newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela to tighten screws on tax cheats - Azocar.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela to tighten screws on tax cheats - Azocar.

text.p: With income tax evasion running at over 50 percent, Venezuela plans to boost its efforts against tax cheats who are costing the country about $2.5 billion a year, Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar said Saturday.
"They know a campaign against those who evade taxes is coming. It's impossible that in this country the only ones who are paying are the fools on the payroll," Matos told a news conference.
Independent workers and those working outside the formal sector of the economy frequently fail to complete tax returns, he said.
Matos said that although there were no precise figures on tax evasion, "some of the estimations point to 1.2 trillion bolivars ($2.5 billion)."
Venezuelan non-oil tax revenues in 1996 totaled 2.5 trillion bolivars ($5.2 billion).
